title: Vulnerability Management Lab
description: End-to-end vulnerability lifecycle on three VulnHub targets — discover, enumerate, triage, validate, remediate, verify.
summary: A hands-on vulnerability management lab performed against three VulnHub targets in an isolated VirtualBox host-only network. The lab walks the full lifecycle — discover → scan → triage → validate → remediation plan → verify — and captures every step as a real artifact. Findings are mapped to specific scan files, screenshots, and triage notes, so each conclusion is traceable to its evidence rather than asserted.
results: Performed full enumeration against EMP, ColddBox, and Hackable II
Identified P1-class findings on each target with reproducible evidence
Validated at least one high-impact finding per asset (e.g. anonymous FTP on Hackable II)
Produced remediation plans with compensating controls
Verified mitigations through follow-up scans

title: SIEM Monitoring & Log Analysis Lab
description: Single-node Wazuh SIEM on a Kali Live USB — manager + indexer + dashboard + local agent, with first-login guide and dashboard proof.
summary: A working, hands-on SIEM lab: Wazuh installed end-to-end on Kali Live USB with encrypted persistence, with the local Kali host enrolled as the first agent. The repo ships the install script, a first-login checklist, and dashboard screenshots proving the stack is up and shipping events. The single-node footprint is intentional — the lab is fully portable and lets the operator stand up a SIEM anywhere a Pi cyberdeck can boot.
results: Deployed a single-node Wazuh stack from a vendored install script
Enrolled the local Kali host as the first reporting agent
Validated event ingestion via the dashboard
Documented the post-install checklist and admin-password rotation

title: Security Toolchain Environment
description: A repeatable framework for verifying that a Kali workstation has the right tools installed, and that they actually work — with reusable wrappers and labbed proof artifacts.
summary: Inventories the tools expected on an offensive-security workstation, wraps the most-used workflows so they run the same way every time, and validates each tool by linking labbed output (real scan results) back to the tool matrix. A tool listed without a `labs/` artifact is treated as unproven.
results: One-shot tool presence check across the expected toolset
Reusable web-enumeration wrapper (nikto + gobuster + ffuf)
Tool matrix mapping each tool to its labbed validation artifact
Documented workflows for web enumeration and offline cracking

title: Security Operations HUD
description: Bash-driven operator HUD for a portable cyberdeck — tmux dashboard, KEY=VALUE status feeds, and one-line controls for network mode, logging, and capture.
summary: A glanceable operator interface for a Pi-based cyberdeck operating in the field. Three things — status producers that emit machine-readable KEY=VALUE blocks (host, CPU, memory, temperature, interface state, channel, active tools), a tmux 4-pane dashboard that watches them, and operator controls that toggle network mode, logging, and capture. No GUI dependencies; sudo-aware so controls degrade gracefully if not root.
results: KEY=VALUE producers for host, network, and tool state
4-pane tmux dashboard (render / tools / net / status)
Sudo-aware operator toggles (managed / monitor / lab modes)
State persisted across reboots via the encrypted persistence partition

title: Encrypted Live Security Environment
description: Bootable Kali Live USB with LUKS-encrypted persistence — your hardened work environment travels in your pocket and stays unreadable if the stick is lost.
summary: A documented, reproducible workflow for building a Kali Live USB with LUKS-encrypted persistence. Boots reliably on commodity hardware, persists data across reboots, and ships sanitized proof artifacts so the build can be reproduced without exposing the operator's specific environment.
results: Bootable Live USB with LUKS-encrypted persistence
Documented build workflow with sanitized proof artifacts
Foundation that every other Brick Stack repo depends on

title: Live USB Auto Time Sync
description: Automatic system time sync the moment a Kali Live USB connects to a network — NetworkManager dispatcher hook + connectivity check + systemd-timesyncd. Validated working.
summary: A Live USB often boots offline or with a stale BIOS clock. That breaks HTTPS cert validation, log accuracy, and time-sensitive security tooling. This brick fixes that with a one-time setup: as soon as a usable network connects, the time syncs automatically. No manual ntpdate, no crons — just a NetworkManager dispatcher hook that runs the pipeline only when there's a real connection.
results: Time syncs automatically the moment a network connects
No daemons or cron required — event-driven only
Sanitized sample log shows real before/after sync deltas
Integrates cleanly with encrypted persistence (Brick #1)

title: System Backup & Recovery Workflow
description: Repeatable, verifiable Linux backup workflow against an external drive — partition → format → mount → rsync → verify — config-driven and machine-agnostic.
summary: Off-the-shelf backup tools either hide what they're doing or assume cloud storage. This brick is the opposite: explicit, scriptable, and produces logs you can show to a security auditor. The drive identifier, partition layout, mount point, and source root all come from a single config file — change one line and the whole pipeline retargets to a different drive. The format step requires typing the literal word ERASE; there is no -y flag.
results: Config-driven runner that retargets via one file
Timestamped proof artifacts on every run (lsblk, parted, rsync, verify)
Explicit ERASE-typed gate prevents accidental wipes
Reproducible across any Linux host

title: Portable Cyberdeck Platform
description: Raspberry Pi 5 cyberdeck — portable, modular, documented, and field-ready. Hardware selection, OS hardening, power, and reproducible build docs.
summary: Turns the persistent OS from Brick #1 into a physical, deployable system that can be operated at a desk, in a lab, or in the field. The emphasis is on hardware integration, mobility, power management, and documentation — not offensive techniques. Brick #1 is the brain; this brick is the body.
results: Portable cybersecurity workstation with stable power profile
Documented hardware BOM and assembly process
OS hardening baseline applied
Networking configured for non-offensive operation

title: Azure Fundamentals — Foundation Cell
description: A reproducible Azure foundation: subscription + budget governance, VNet with segmented subnets, NSG controls, and a validated VM with stop-deallocate discipline.
summary: A from-zero Azure environment built like a real engineering exercise: every architectural decision is recorded, every step is screenshot-proven, and cost governance is treated as a first-class requirement. The environment is the foundation layer that subsequent cells (security hardening, monitoring, detection, automation) build on top of. Public exposure status: none.
results: Subscription activated with budget guardrails on day 1
VNet with enterprise-style subnet segmentation
NSG-attached subnets with no public exposure
Validated Ubuntu VM deployment, then stopped/deallocated for cost discipline
40+ proof screenshots covering every step

title: Azure Security Hardening & Monitoring
description: End-to-end Azure security: NSG IP allowlisting, key-only SSH, Log Analytics + AMA + DCR, KQL detections for SSH success / failure / brute-force, and alert rules.
summary: Provision → Harden → Monitor → Detect → Respond → Improve. Stand up infrastructure (Cell A), harden it (NSG /32 allowlisting, SSH key-only), instrument it (Log Analytics + Azure Monitor Agent + Data Collection Rule for LOG_AUTH/LOG_AUTHPRIV), write KQL detections (heartbeat, SSH success / failure, brute-force ≥5 failures in 5 minutes), configure alerts (`ssh-bruteforce-5in5m`, `heartbeat-stale-5m`), and verify by exercising the alerts.
results: Inbound SSH restricted to a single /32 source
Password auth disabled; SSH key-only enforced
Linux auth logs centralized into Log Analytics
KQL detections covering SSH success, failure, and brute-force
Two Sev-3 alerts firing on real telemetry

title: Airpoint — Touchless Cursor (Computer Vision)
description: Touchless cursor control via webcam — 15+ hand gestures, PyQt5 GUI, system tray, fully offline. Privacy-first: no network calls, no telemetry.
summary: Move your mouse, click, scroll, and drag — all with hand gestures, using just your webcam. No hardware modifications, no cloud processing, no telemetry. The hand-tracking model runs locally and the application requires zero internet access during normal use. Cross-platform (Linux / macOS / Windows) with one-liner install scripts and a full GUI control panel for sensitivity, smoothing, and gesture toggles.
results: 15+ recognized gestures (click, double-click, right-click, scroll, drag, volume / media control)
Cross-platform install scripts for Linux, macOS, and Windows
GUI control panel with live preview, sliders, and gesture toggles
System tray integration with start/stop/quit menu
Camera auto-recovery on unplug/replug
Zero network calls during normal operation

title: Local AI Web Workspace
description: Local-first AI workspace: Ollama + AnythingLLM + Homarr behind a single docker compose. Cross-platform bootstrap. No cloud account required.
summary: Run your own AI models on your own machine, with a clean browser-based interface. The stack pairs Ollama (running natively on the host for inference) with AnythingLLM (browser chat UI in Docker) and Homarr (dashboard / landing page in Docker), wired together so AnythingLLM talks to Ollama on the right host bridge for each platform. Cross-platform bootstrap scripts install Docker and Ollama if missing, and a sanitization workflow keeps real environment values out of the public repo.
results: One-command bootstrap installs Docker + Ollama on Linux / macOS / Windows
Three-service stack (Homarr / AnythingLLM / Ollama) with correct cross-platform host bridging
Optional extras (code-server, WeTTY, Filebrowser) as separate compose files
Sanitization checklist enforces no real secrets or hostnames in the public repo

title: VaultKeeper — Encrypted Knowledge Platform
description: Local-first, end-to-end encrypted knowledge platform — Tauri desktop + React Native mobile + Rust (Axum) sync server on a Pi. XChaCha20-Poly1305, SQLite FTS5, D3 graph view.
summary: An Obsidian-style knowledge platform that puts the user in control of their data. Notes are stored as plain markdown on the device, encrypted client-side with XChaCha20-Poly1305 (libsodium) before optional sync, and synced to a Raspberry Pi running a Rust Axum server in Docker. Cross-platform: Tauri (desktop) + React Native (mobile) sharing a Rust crypto/sync core.
results: Monorepo with shared TypeScript types, crypto, and sync-protocol packages
Tauri desktop app with TipTap editor, command palette, D3 graph view
React Native mobile app
Rust sync server with JWT + Argon2id auth
Docker / Nginx / Tailscale deployment templates
